plate_findings.evidence: Caption: "Hyper- and hypo-pigmented skin of neck and upper chest."

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Clinical photograph of an adult male with the captioned nail-dystrophy manifestation of DKC1-related dyskeratosis congenita. [raw subtype: DKC1-related (X-linked) dyskeratosis congenita] B: Clinical photograph showing the characteristic mottled hyper- and hypopigmentation of the neck and upper chest in the captioned adult with DKC1-related dyskeratosis congenita. [raw subtype: DKC1-related (X-linked) dyskeratosis congenita] C: Clinical photograph showing irregular tongue leukoplakia, a specific mucocutaneous manifestation attributed by the caption to the patient's DKC1-related dyskeratosis congenita. [raw subtype: DKC1-related (X-linked) dyskeratosis congenita]

panels.figure_caption: Mucocutaneous features of dyskeratosis congenita of an adult male whose disease is due to a DKC1 mutation. ( A) Dystrophic and ridged fingernails. ( B) Hyper- and hypo-pigmented skin of neck and upper chest. ( C) Irregular leukoplakia of the tongue.
in_text_mentions: DC was first described in a 1906 case report of males with the mucocutaneous triad of abnormal skin pigmentation, nail dystrophy, and oral leukoplakia ( Figure 2) 1. Additional similar cases were reported, including the first female case in 1963 2– 5.
